newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU seen needing to export more grain in 96/97 - ZMP.
newsitem.headline: EU seen needing to export more grain in 96/97 - ZMP.

text.p: European Union (EU) cereals managers needed to ease pressure on the internal markets by maintaining a strong presence in competitive export areas, German farm price office ZMP wrote on Friday.
An article in ZMP's weekly grain and oilseeds report said, "There is no alternative to higher exports in 96/97 compared with last year," EU exports totalled 18 million last season.
Otherwise, unwanted grain would end up in intervention stores, which had just been successfully wound down.
ZMP said importers such as Brazil, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Egypt and Taiwan were in need of grain, but higher world harvests in general meant a higher self-sufficiency rate.
This was adding to the competitive tone in export markets -- already expressed in an EU export rebate as high as 22.35 Ecus a tonne for free market wheat on Nov 7, ZMP said.
But with trade complaints from the U.S. looming if the EU got too generous with subsidies, the restitution at the weekly tender on Nov 14 was already lowered to 15.97 Ecus.
The EU was also under internal pressure from British free marketeers to cut export refunds, while Germany supported them and France was somewhere in the middle.
EU wheat export commitments since July were down at 3.049 million tonnes against 2.697 million last year on Nov 12, not counting Thursday's 256,500 tonnes.
ZMP saw downward price pressure on EU wheat from lower Chicago wheat and maize levels and because an ample domestic maize crop helps replaced feed wheat in animal food rations.
Maize farmgate prices in southern Germany at 225 marks a tonne were down 15 percent from last year, it noted.

But lower world wheat market prices could be good news for quality EU wheat, which attracts a premium over normal baking qualities, as wheat import tariffs into the EU would fall and consumers turn to domestic wheat.

ZMP estimated Germany's domestic grain use in 1996/97 at 35.40 million tonnes from a 41.98 million tonne crop, compared with a 35.19 million tonne consumption in 95/96 from a 39.22 million tonne crop.
